newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-QUEENSLAND PUSH FOR SHIELD FINAL BERTH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-QUEENSLAND PUSH FOR SHIELD FINAL BERTH.

text.p: Queensland improved their claim for a place in the Sheffield Shield final by moving to the verge of victory against South Australia on Saturday.
The Queenslanders reduced their opponents to 193 for nine in their second innings at close of play on the third day at the Gabba and need to claim one more wicket to secure a vital win.
The visitors face the daunting task of needing to add a further 143 runs for the last wicket to deny Queensland.
But depending on results elsewhere, a victory in Brisbane may not be enough to earn Queensland a trip to Perth to face Shield leaders Western Australia in the five-day final next week.
Tasmania will secure second place on the table behind Western Australia and a final berth at Queensland's expense if they beat New South Wales at the Sydney Cricket Ground on Sunday.
At close of play on day three, Tasmania were 135 for no wicket, a lead of 149 runs, with one day remaining and all their second innings wickets in hand.
New South Wales earlier compiled a total of 449 in reply to the visitors' first innings 463 for seven declared.
Veteran New South Wales wicketkeeper Phil Emery scored 100 not out, his maiden first-class century in his 100th first-class game.
In Melbourne, Western Australia proved their readiness for the final by taking a firm grip of their match against Victoria.
At close of play on day three, Victoria were 108 for four in their second innings, still needing 145 runs to avoid an innings defeat.
